history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration establish a periodic control mechanism to recover the costs of the services rendered, with the purpose of avoiding delays in the payments from its clients.
history.administration_response: The United Nations Office at Vienna put in place a system whereby internal and external clients are billed in advance of the period to which the services relate. In addition, there is an established process in place to monitor the collection of receivables. The Accounts Section of the Office’s Financial Resources Management Service periodically runs an Umoja report on accounts receivable report to monitor the status of the Office’s receivables. Subsequently, the Accounts Section follows-up on any pending accounts receivable. All the invoices, correspondences and reminders are stored, with each customer having a separate folder. All communications are also centralized in a single email account. In 2023, all initial yearly invoices were cleared (paid) by the end of January, except one payment cleared in the first week of February. Overall, the Office has made substantive progress related to timely collection of payments from service recipients, whereby related income was collected within an average of one month of service start date compared to over seven months in 2022.
history.board_assessment: The Board verified that the United Nations Office at Vienna, for the purpose of avoiding delays in the payments from its clients, put in place new control and monitoring practices on this matter, such as initiating prompt negotiations with its respective clients and requiring from them the necessary information to collect the associated cost recoveries in a timely manner. Regarding the above, the Board verified that the Office had developed a follow-up spreadsheet document as a control mechanism, which contained, among others, client’s data on the services and its related costs, negotiation and confirmation dates, and payment dates and documents. Additionally, the Board verified that there were no delays in the payments. In almost all cases, clients paid before the end of January 2023, and only two of them paid in February and March of the same year. Finally, the Office confirmed that the spreadsheet document was used as a control mechanism and that the above-mentioned activities will be extended beyond 2023. In view of the above, the Board considers this recommendation to be implemented.
